title: Preface
summary:
UNCLASSIFIED
OFFICE OF THE DIRECTOR OF NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE
Preliminary Assessment: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena
25 June 2021
UNCLASSIFIEDUNCLASSIFIED

title: SCOPE AND ASSUMPTIONS
summary: ODNI preliminary report, responding to Senate Report 116-233 for FY2021 IAA, assesses the threat from unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP) and progress of the DoD UAP Task Force. It gives policymakers the challenges of characterizing UAP and aims to develop processes, policies, technologies, and training for personnel encountering UAP. Data covers mainly USG reports from November 2004 to March 2021, still being collected. Assumes sensors operate correctly, though some UAP may be sensor anomalies. Drafted with input from many agencies.

title: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
summary: The UAPTF found limited high-quality reporting on UAP, so it built a tailored reporting process and focused on 2004-2021 reports. Most UAP likely are physical objects, seen across multiple sensors. A few showed unusual flight traits, possibly from sensor error, spoofing, or misperception. Likely five explanatory categories: airborne clutter, natural atmospheric phenomena, US developmental programs, foreign adversary systems, and other. UAP pose flight safety and possible national security concerns. Better data consolidation and analysis are recommended, though some steps need investment.

title: AVAILABLE REPORTING LARGELY INCONCLUSIVE
summary: The text covers UAP (unidentified aerial phenomena) reporting from 2004-2021, mostly from military aviators. Reporting was inconsistent until the Navy's March 2019 mechanism, later adopted by the Air Force in 2020; 144 USG reports exist, 80 with multiple sensors, and only one (a deflating balloon) was identified. Collection is hampered by stigma, sensor limitations, and vantage point issues. Patterns cluster by shape, size, and propulsion, and near training grounds (possibly collection bias). In 18 incidents, UAP showed unusual movement, and a few data sets suggest advanced technology, requiring further expert analysis.

title: UAP PROBABLY LACK A SINGLE EXPLANATION
summary: Describes a UAP dataset analysis concluding UAP likely have multiple explanations, not one. Incidents may fall into five categories: airborne clutter (one case, a deflating balloon, identified with high confidence), natural atmospheric phenomena (ice, moisture, thermal effects), USG or industry developmental programs (unconfirmed), foreign adversary systems, and an 'other' category pending scientific advances. The UAPTF will focus on cases with unusual flight or signature management.

title: UAP THREATEN FLIGHT SAFETY AND, POSSIBLY, NATIONAL SECURITY
summary: Summarizes a UAP (unidentified aerial phenomena) report: UAP pose flight-safety hazards and possibly national security risks, such as foreign collection programs or adversary aerospace breakthroughs. Aviators must report hazards, but range incursions can halt tests and deter reporting. The UAPTF has 11 documented pilot near-miss reports. No data yet links UAP to foreign programs or advanced adversary technology, though monitoring continues since some were seen near military facilities or by advanced USG sensor aircraft.

title: EXPLAINING UAP WILL REQUIRE ANALYTIC, COLLECTION AND RESOURCE INVESTMENT
summary: The UAPTF aims to widen UAP analysis to more USG personnel and technical systems, using AI/ML to cluster patterns and pre-screen reports against known aerial objects. It is building interagency workflows, standardizing reporting across military services, and acquiring Navy, USAF (six-month pilot since Nov 2020), and FAA data. It also seeks radar historical data to reduce collection bias, updates its collection strategy, and calls for R&D investment guided by a Collection Strategy, Technical Roadmap, and Program Plan.

title: APPENDIX A - Definition of Key Terms
summary: Defines key UAP terms: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (broadest category of airborne objects reviewed), UAP Event (holistic description of a pilot/aircrew sighting or detection), UAP Incident (specific part of an event), and UAP Report (documentation with chain of custody, time, date, location, and description, including Range Fouler reports). Footnote defines 'range fouler' as an object or activity interrupting military training or operations in restricted airspace or military operating areas.

title: APPENDIX B – Senate Report Accompanying the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021
summary: Appendix B summarizes Senate Report 116-233 for the FY2021 Intelligence Authorization Act. It directs the DNI, with SECDEF and other agencies, to assess the threat from unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP) and the UAPTF's progress. Requested content: analysis of ONI and UAPTF UAP data; analysis of GEOINT, SIGINT, HUMINT, and MASINT UAP data; FBI investigation data on restricted airspace intrusions; a centralized interagency reporting process with an accountable official; assessment of threats and possible foreign adversary attribution; signs of adversary breakthrough aerospace capabilities; and recommendations on collection, R&D, and funding.
